How do I start using SubHub?

The Dom sets the scene. During setup, choose individual apps or All Apps, then complete Android access setup. The Dom can change the shared selection in Settings → Apps and set the rules on each feature’s page.\n\nOn Home, choose a service duration and tap Enter Service. Lock Dom controls to hand over to the Sub. Turning a feature off keeps its page available to the Dom, ready for a change of plans.
Who holds the reins: Dom or Sub?

The Dom holds the reins: apps, Censor, Limits, tribute rules, Rituals, and service duration. The Sub follows the saved arrangement, sees the service dashboard, and uses permitted actions. The header’s Unlock control opens Dom access with the Dom PIN or keyholder code. Protected actions stay marked and ask you to unlock; tapping them does not open a PIN dialog.\n\nKeyholder on Rituals belongs to the Dom. Its Authenticator can pair a remote Dom using a compatible authenticator app. App Lock and the screen privacy filter protect access or visibility; neither grants Dom authorization.
When does the Sub get released?

Enter Service puts the Dom’s rules to work. The Dom must authorize Leave Service for both timed and permanent service. Timed service ends automatically at its deadline. Your last duration selection and Random bounds remain selected after service and when you reopen the app. Switching between Dom and Sub does not end a running service or erase its settings.\n\nAndroid can interrupt background access, and Screen Capture needs fresh Android approval for each session. Check the Home status after restarting the device. During timed service, Home shows a countdown clock instead of duration choices. Hide Countdown keeps the ring but hides the time; Censor Off uses blur. Permanent service shows an infinity symbol in the same panel.
Which apps does SubHub affect?

Settings → Apps is the shared selection for Censor, Limits, Subliminal Messaging, and Popup Storm. All Apps overrides the scope, including eligible launchable apps you install later, without changing your saved selection. Turn it off to use that selection again. Essential Android screens, keyboards, and SubHub itself are excluded where needed.\n\nSelecting apps does not enable a disabled feature. Per-app Limits allowances are configured on Limits. Removing an app does not erase usage already counted toward today’s combined budget.
Which Android access do I need?

Accessibility supplies foreground-app changes and the live controls used by App Mode and Limits. Display over other apps allows visible overlays. On Android 13 and newer, notification permission lets SubHub show its ongoing status. Android permission buttons in Settings are available in either Dom or Sub.\n\nThe Access Guide explains restricted Accessibility settings step by step. Screen Capture and Censor Lab recording require separate Android approval. Hardcore requests Device Admin separately; ordinary censoring does not require it.
How does the Dom cover temptation?

The Dom decides what stays under wraps. On Censor, choose Low, Medium, or High detection to enable it, or Off to disable it. Detection coverage and censor appearance are separate choices; changing the look does not change the detection level.\n\nCensor works on supported visible images and text in selected apps while service is running. Secure windows and some Android surfaces cannot be captured. Gallery Censor handles chosen files separately.
How much playtime does the Sub get?

The Dom decides when playtime ends. Limits has separate controls for per-app allowances and the combined daily budget. Enable either or both. There is no additional feature switch. If both apply, the smaller remaining allowance decides how much time the Sub gets.\n\nUsage resets at local midnight. When an applicable budget runs out, SubHub returns the covered app to Home. Limits needs Accessibility; Screen Capture alone cannot track and enforce foreground-app time.
When does temptation earn tribute?

The Dom sets the price of temptation. Enable the individual rules you want in Wallet. Any enabled rule can run during service; turning all rules off stops new rule-based tributes. Wallet has no separate enable switch. Set prices, batching, correction time, and daily or weekly caps before starting.\n\nTributes are recorded locally until payment is authorized. Paid Pause has its own offer checkbox and price and can run independently. Turning off tribute rules does not remove existing Wallet history or unpaid amounts.
How do I connect PayPal?

The Dom opens Wallet → PayPal. Select Sandbox for testing or Live for real payments, then connect the matching PayPal REST app credentials. Live and Sandbox credentials and wallets are separate.\n\nA saved payer wallet requires PayPal Vault capability for the merchant app and the payer’s approval through PayPal. Linking a wallet does not charge it. Manual checkout requires the payer to approve payment. Check connection and wallet status on the PayPal tab before relying on a payment method.
What does Hardcore change?

Hardcore adds Android-supported friction to protected uninstall, data-clear, and settings paths while service is active. It uses Device Admin and Dom authorization for release. It does not make Android impossible to bypass. Keep the Dom PIN and a recovery path available.\n\nSaved-wallet automatic payment is a separate, explicit choice. It also requires an active service lock, Hardcore, applicable Wallet rules, and a verified saved wallet. PayPal may decline a payment or ask the payer to authorize again.
Where does the Dom add a little tease?

Rituals contains Packs, Gallery Censor, Subliminal Messaging, Popup Storm, Achievements, and the Dom-only Keyholder page. Open Subliminal Messaging or Popup Storm to enable or disable that effect and edit its settings. Both use the shared Apps selection during service.\n\nIf Popup Storm is uncomfortable, use its safety stop. Statistics remain on Home. Arrangement summaries show configured counts even when a feature is off; they are not proof that service is running.
What happens to Gallery originals?

Gallery Censor on Rituals puts selected images or videos under wraps by creating censored copies. The Sub can choose media and adjust output quality, video settings, audio, or original deletion; the Dom controls Look and Censor Areas. Review the preview and output settings before exporting. An export uses the settings chosen when it starts, even if live settings change later.\n\nExports can continue in the background and show saved progress or results when you return. Original files remain unless you explicitly choose deletion. Review an exported copy before deleting an original.
What can a pack change?

Packs on Rituals lets you make, import, review, and share .sub arrangements. Editing a draft does not change the running setup. The Dom reviews the selected sections before applying them and can restore the previous settings.\n\nA pack cannot grant Android access, start service, change the Dom PIN, or import the shared Apps list. Merchant credentials can be included only with explicit encrypted sharing; share those packs and their passphrase only with trusted recipients. Payer consent and payment history remain local.
Why is a feature not working?

Check that service is running, the app is included, the feature’s own controls are enabled, and Android access is granted. For Limits, check the applicable allowance. For Wallet, check the rule and caps. For Censor, check that detection is not Off.\n\nDiagnostics shows actual service and detector state, timing, and recent errors. Censor Lab lives inside Diagnostics. Both are available to the Sub; changing the diagnostics overlay requires Dom. Lab recording starts only after you approve Android screen capture. Stop remains available during recording. Review recordings before sharing: they may contain visible screen content. A permission being granted does not prove that the live service is connected.
What stays on this device?

Image and text detection run on this device. Ordinary screen snapshots are processed in memory rather than saved. Settings, selected apps, statistics, arrangements, Wallet history, and diagnostics remain local unless you export or share them.\n\nCensor Lab saves a recording only after Android approval and does not record microphone audio. PayPal credentials and saved-wallet identifiers use Android Keystore protection; authorization, checkout, and risk data are sent to PayPal. Updates contact GitHub. Stable updates are the default; development updates are opt-in. Downloads require your tap and installation requires Android approval.
